description:
The value of lifting the SemanticClosed barrier (fz-bfh.5.5 steps 2-4: co-settling transport pre-seal) is incremental-recompilation blast-radius -- and NO test exercises it. The engine's rebase/contribution semantics are tested generically (scheduler_test.rs:615+: cumulative ascent vs replacing-rebase vs retraction), but nothing edits a source, re-drives the SAME world, and asserts which transport facts (ExecutableTransport(E)/TransportPlan) re-settle vs stay cached. The full matrix + shadow + contract tests all run a single batch drive to a sealed closure.

Build that signal: a harness that drives a root to settle, applies a localized source edit, re-drives, and asserts (via telemetry/fact revisions) that only the affected executables' transport facts re-settled. Without it, steps 2-4 of fz-bfh.5.5 produce a byte-identical BATCH plan (verifiable) but their actual purpose -- pre-seal/incremental co-settling -- is unverifiable, so landing the contribution-fact machinery would be non-load-bearing complexity until an unverifiable gate-drop. This is northstar 'add measurements for signal' and is really fz-rh2 (incremental spine) territory. Blocks the value-bearing remainder of fz-bfh.5.5.

comments.text:
DESIGN (investigated, code-grounded):
- NO source-edit/invalidate primitive exists: world.submit_code -> code.define always mints a NEW CodeId; there is no redefine/replace_code/invalidate. So the signal cannot be 'edit function F'. It must use incremental ADDITION that grows an EXISTING root's closure (production path), or a new production edit primitive must be built first (fz-rh2 spine).
- Observable: per-job telemetry span ["fz","compiler2","job"] (drive.rs:193) carries metadata job=opaque_debug(&job). Capture + filter metadata_str(event,"job").starts_with("DeriveExecutableTransport") and count per drive() call. fact_revision(key) (world.rs:2574) is the content-revision signal (secondary; facts are content-addressed so unrelated content revs may already be stable).
- RED->GREEN mechanism (traced): derive_executable_transport(E) currently READS SemanticClosed(root). Growing the closure re-runs SealSemanticClosure -> define_semantic_closure changed=true -> SemanticClosed revision bumps -> scheduler rebases ALL readers -> every DeriveExecutableTransport(E) re-runs (RED: unaffected execs re-derive). After the lift (5.5 step 4) the per-exec job reads only E's own prereqs (ActivationAnalyzed/RuntimeDemand/InputSources contributions), so unrelated growth rebases nothing -> unaffected execs' transport jobs do NOT re-run (GREEN).
- Test shape: drive 1 settles root main (capture DeriveExecutableTransport run-set S1); submit additional code that grows main's SAME closure; drive 2 (capture run-set S2); assert an executable provably unaffected by the addition is in S1 but NOT in S2.
- OPEN design crux: construct a closure that cleanly SETTLES then GROWS via production primitives. New-root or two-roots-sharing-a-helper does NOT exercise it (ExecutableTransport(E) is root-independent; a new root's growth doesn't bump the old root's SemanticClosed). Needs main to NEWLY reach an executable on the second drive -- candidate mechanisms: deferred function definition (call present in drive 1 but definition submitted in drive 2) or an incrementally-added defimpl that an existing polymorphic call site newly resolves to. Verify the drive-1 state settles (TransportPlan present) with the not-yet-reached target.

title: Incremental-recompilation signal: test transport facts re-settle with bounded blast-radius
